articles.title: Monastic Field House / ROOMOOR
articles.summary: Around 2005, a devout family donated a parcel of land on the highway near Surat at Baleshwar for the construction of a Jain temple and its ancillary structures such as dharamshalas (accommodation), bhojanshala (community kitchen and dining hall), and vyakhyan kendra (spiritual discourse hall). As a token of appreciation, the presiding head monk promised the family a small private lot within the precinct. The family chose to build a house twenty years later.

articles.title: Companion Villa / AsNow Design & Construct
articles.summary: Companion Villa is a residential project that responds to the challenges of density, scale, and neighborhood context while maintaining a minimalist modernist language.

articles.title: Piedra Bay House / U-Guide Space Design Atelier
articles.summary: At Casa Piedra Bay, the landscape is not simply contemplated; it becomes an essential part of the experience of inhabiting the house. Located in Palmar de Ocoa , Azua, Dominican Republic, the project emerges from an arid coastal setting defined by the contrast between the mountains and the Caribbean Sea. The architecture responds to this environment through a spatial composition that prioritizes natural ventilation, filtered sunlight, privacy, and a continuous connection with the surrounding landscape.

articles.title: M38 House / Muda Prefab
articles.summary: The M38 House is born from a question: how can we industrialize construction without standardizing architecture? This 38 m² prefabricated house aligns domestic space design with manufacturing, transportation, and assembly processes. Its first unit is installed inside the workshop where it was built, serving as a showroom that allows visitors to experience the spaces and learn about the house's materials within its manufacturing context.

articles.title: Espiga House / Grupo Primitivo
articles.summary: Vivienda Espiga explores the potential of the structure as an organizing and qualifying element of architectural space, transcending its role as mere support to become the primary articulator of the living experience. Through a sequence of timber structural frames, the project establishes an order that defines pathways, articulates rooms, and builds a material identity where structure, architecture, and landscape integrate into a single expression.

articles.title: MUZEU – Thought and Contemporary Art / Carvalho Araújo
articles.summary: MUZEU transforms the former Judicial Court of Braga into a new space dedicated to contemporary art and thought. The project preserves the existing facades and integrates the 14th-century medieval wall, reorganizing the interior through a new contemporary structure.

articles.title: Courtyard House / Hennessey Architecture
articles.summary: For this modestly-scaled renovation of a classic suburban Mill Valley house, the home was thought not only as a shelter, but also as a bridge: from past to present; from one landscape condition to another; and from what a family wanted to what they could have. Designed for a couple with two young children, the house is meant to support their current needs as a young family and grow with them.

articles.title: Cabin Budor / R21 Arkitekter
articles.summary: The commission consists of the design and construction of a weekend cabin in Budor. The main challenge is to integrate the volume into the landscape through its materiality, seeking to ensure that the project interferes as little as possible with the natural surroundings. The architecture aims to establish a dialogue with the landscape without attempting to dominate it.

articles.title: The Simple, Beautiful Interface on Braun's 1960s Portable Heater
articles.summary: In the mid-1960s, Dieter Rams and Reinhold Weiss designed Braun's H7, a portable fan and heater. It had one fan setting, and two heat settings.
